evals.prompt: A user asks to add retries to payment callbacks. Counts, final failure state and duplicate-event behavior are undefined. A retry-count answer reveals that callbacks may arrive out of order. Clarify before implementing.
evals.expected_output: Build and update a dependency graph including order state, idempotency and final failure. Investigate existing facts, ask one frontier decision with a recommendation, and retain blocked readiness until critical downstream choices close. Do not implement.

evals.prompt: The requirements Command is active. After three questions the user has not decided whether a failed migration deletes source records. A first slice and one acceptance criterion already exist. The operator wants progress.
evals.expected_output: Report the deletion/recovery choice as critical and open, preserve blocked readiness, show safe independent investigation and the exact pending decision. Three questions, a first slice and assumptions-recorded cannot authorize destructive behavior or complete clarification.

evals.prompt: The accepted user request specifies all report behavior and authorizes implementation. Only newest-first versus oldest-first sorting is unspecified and either passes the same accepted criteria. Existing source inspection supports feasibility.
evals.expected_output: Record an explicit low-impact reversible sorting default with rationale, reuse accepted user instructions for confirmed alignment, cite happy/failure walkthroughs and inspection evidence, and return a ready typed decision without asking for duplicate approval or invoking implementation.

evals.prompt: A proposed workflow reads messages, changes a record and promises automatic rollback. The record-write API is documented, but rollback support is unknown and no probe has run. The user has approved the intended outcome.
evals.expected_output: Walk the happy and partial-failure paths, identify rollback as a critical feasibility dependency, inspect available APIs or run a minimal authorized probe, and remain blocked if unsupported. Product alignment alone does not prove the workflow can run.

evals.prompt: There are two open decisions: where data is stored, and whether the selected store supports retention. Retention depends on storage. A third independent naming decision is also open. The agent has not yet read the repository configuration.
evals.expected_output: Read the configuration for facts, represent the storage-to-retention dependency, ask one currently answerable decision with a recommendation, then recompute the frontier. Do not ask the user facts available in files, silently resolve retention or batch dependent questions.

evals.prompt: A previously accepted requirements decision is persisted. A new user message changes external notification behavior. You can add a readiness field to historical unfinished decisions, but the current behavior change is not part of the original scope.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the accepted decision, report the new goal as a new workflow requirement and do not rewrite the old decision under readiness enrichment. Record authorized alignment from actual messages rather than inventing it.

evals.prompt: A nightly import proposal says read the feed, merge results and notify. It has no behavior for empty feeds, repeated inputs or a notification failure after a successful merge. Someone claims the spec is done because all seven template fields are filled.
evals.expected_output: Challenge the completion claim with an end-to-end and failure walkthrough, expand the downstream state/duplicate/notification decisions, separate factual investigation from user choices, and keep critical gaps blocked despite template completeness. Avoid imposing a scheduler or AI when unnecessary.

evals.prompt: A legacy requirements document is readable but lacks readiness. The user says continue the same task, and previous instructions already resolve the desired behavior. Available tests demonstrate the relevant interface; no new user choice is needed.
evals.expected_output: Reuse prior authorization and accepted scope, add real decision dependencies and walkthrough/feasibility refs, and submit the enriched typed readiness record for the current Command. Do not treat legacy evidence alone as ready, demand a new approval, fabricate a probe or start the next Provider.
